target_customer: Robotics companies and labs that need human demonstration data to train robot policies
problem: Robot learning is bottlenecked by scarce, expensive and low variety demonstration data, since teleoperation needs robots costing $40,000 or more and lab-bound collection. Sensei sells data collected by paid operators using a low-cost device.
business_model: Data collection service, per request pricing, plus hardware and a marketplace of paid operators

founders.name: Anubhav Guha
education: MIT robotics PhD program (left to found Sensei)
founders.background_notes: Chief Engineer and Program Manager on the Aurora DARPA AlphaDogfight team per the YC page.

founders.name: John Piotti
founders.background_notes: Robotics engineer at Aurora, later led reinforcement learning efforts there; earlier full-stack developer at UtilityAPI.

technical_complexity.rationale: Low cost wearable or exoskeleton style capture hardware plus a marketplace for operators; real hardware and data quality work but no research breakthrough needed, and the team was two people.

defensibility.rationale: Data collected for customers is custom per request and a network of operators takes time to build, but hardware and the operator model can be copied by well funded data vendors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No dated evidence of an incumbent move at founding. Later robotics data vendors such as XDOF (launched October 2024 per a June 2026 SiliconANGLE report) entered the same space.

market_need_then: The launch post argues data scarcity is the main bottleneck in robot AI and that teleoperation fleets of 5 to 20 collectors are slow and costly. Demand is asserted by the company, not shown by customer numbers.

identity.logo: Simple wordmark with light and dark variants (company site)
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly and approachable, 'teach robots to be human'

branding.brand_signature: Operators are called 'Senseis', which turns the name into a role for contractors (YC launch post)

brand_strength.rationale: Name is short and ties to the operator role, but no press or community evidence about the brand was found.

outcome_analysis: Sensei is an active two person YC S24 company selling robot training data collected by paid operators. No outcome events were found, no round could be verified beyond aggregator listings, and the market of robotics data vendors grew crowded after its batch. It is too early to call it a success or a failure.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators (CB Insights, VCBacked, TheCompanyCheck) list about $500K pre-seed or seed with Y Combinator as investor, with conflicting round labels and dates (June or September 2024). No company or press confirmation, so no round recorded. No dated 2024 competitors found; XDOF and others appear later and are discussed in outcome_analysis only. Outcome search found only unrelated companies named Sensei.
